skills.name: mattpocock-codex:ask-matt
skills.description: Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.

interface.shortDescription: Find the right skill or workflow

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:chief-of-staff
skills.description: Pursue a long-running goal in a single session by co-ordinating subagents.

interface.shortDescription: Pursue a long-running goal in a single session by co-ordinating subagents

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:code-review
skills.description: Review changes since a commit, branch, tag, or merge-base against repository standards and the originating spec. Report both axes separately. Use for a branch, PR, work-in-progress review, or "review since X".

interface.shortDescription: Review a diff on standards and spec

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:codebase-design
skills.description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

interface.shortDescription: Vocabulary for deep-module design

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:diagnosing-bugs
skills.description: Diagnose hard, recurring, or unclear bugs and performance regressions. Use for explicit diagnosis/debugging requests or when a focused inspection and existing check do not establish the cause.

interface.shortDescription: Diagnose hard bugs and regressions

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:domain-modeling
skills.description: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a GLOSSARY.md, or recording or editing an ADR.

interface.shortDescription: Build and sharpen a domain model

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:grill-me
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.

interface.shortDescription: Sharpen a plan through interview

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:grill-with-docs
skills.description: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.

interface.shortDescription: Grill a design and write its docs

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:grilling
skills.description: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.

interface.shortDescription: Stress-test thinking a round of questions at a time

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:handoff
skills.description: Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.

interface.shortDescription: Compact a conversation into a handoff

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:implement
skills.description: Implement one approved ticket or a small plan retained in the current conversation. Never implement a published spec before to-tickets splits it.

interface.shortDescription: Build one ticket or small same-session plan

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:implement-spec
skills.description: Implements an approved spec and ticket graph with subagents in isolated worktrees, then validates their combined work on one integration branch. Use after /to-spec and /to-tickets.

interface.shortDescription: Implement the result of /to-spec and /to-tickets in code.

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:improve-codebase-architecture
skills.description: Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.

interface.shortDescription: Find and grill architecture improvements

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:pr
skills.description: Use when writing a PR body.

interface.shortDescription: Write a PR body that's fast to review

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:prototype
skills.description: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.

interface.shortDescription: Prototype to answer a design question

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:research
skills.description: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.

interface.shortDescription: Research from high-trust sources

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:retro
skills.description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

interface.shortDescription: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:setup-matt-pocock-skills
skills.description: Configure repository issue tracking, domain docs, review guidance and local commit checks. Run before the engineering workflow, or to update an existing setup.

interface.shortDescription: Configure repo docs and local checks

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:tdd
skills.description: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

interface.shortDescription: Test-driven red-green-refactor

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:teach
skills.description: Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.

interface.shortDescription: Learn a concept in a guided workspace

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:to-questionnaire
skills.description: Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.

interface.shortDescription: Front-load questions into a doc for someone to answer

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:to-spec
skills.description: Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.

interface.shortDescription: Turn a conversation into a spec

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:to-tickets
skills.description: Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker (edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker).

interface.shortDescription: Split a plan into tracer-bullet tickets

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:triage
skills.description: Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles, categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.

interface.shortDescription: Move issues through triage roles

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:wait-what
skills.description: Stop. That last message did not land: re-pitch it.

interface.shortDescription: Re-pitch that: simpler, with the context I'm missing

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:wayfinder
skills.description: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

interface.shortDescription: Map a large effort as decision tickets

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:wizard
skills.description: Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.

interface.shortDescription: Generate an interactive setup wizard

skills.name: mattpocock-codex:writing-for-agents
skills.description: Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

interface.shortDescription: Write documents agents consume

skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.shortDescription: Generate or edit images for websites, games, and more
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $imagegen to make or edit an image for this project.

skills.name: openai-docs
skills.description: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex.
skills.shortDescription: Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, and self-knowledge; OpenAI APIs and ChatGPT Work. 'You'/'this app' means Codex only.

interface.shortDescription: OpenAI and Codex docs for models, skills, tasks, and setup
interface.defaultPrompt: Use OpenAI Docs for official docs lookup, questions about Codex itself or Codex surfaces, model selection, model migration, and prompt-upgrade work.

skills.name: review-agent
skills.description: Perform a read-only, defect-first review of a specified code change and return every actionable finding. Use when another agent delegates review of uncommitted changes, a base-branch diff, a commit, or custom review instructions.

interface.shortDescription: Find actionable bugs in code changes
interface.defaultPrompt: Use $review-agent to review the requested code changes and return actionable findings.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources.

interface.shortDescription: Create or update a skill

skills.name: skill-installer
skills.description: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos).
skills.shortDescription: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos

interface.shortDescription: Install curated skills from openai/skills or other repos
